text: Maya Chen, 41-year-old Asian female (5'5", 150 lbs). Stated health goals: more energy, lose ~10 lbs, clearer skin. Practices Functional Medicine and wears an OURA Ring. Chief presentation maps to low energy / fatigue.
Medical history: anxiety disorder. No surgeries. Allergy: nuts (reaction: hives). No prescription medications. Supplements: magnesium glycinate 200mg and vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Family history: mother has an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism); father has type 2 (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes.

Lifestyle: owner of a small screen-printing studio; self-rated work stress 8/10. Exercises 2 days/week; ~20 min of sunlight 3 days/week. Drinks alcohol monthly; no tobacco or recreational drugs. Eats out more than twice a week. Sleep: averages less than 6 hours, does not wake refreshed, wakes about twice per night (once to urinate); unsure about snoring or apnea.

Environmental exposures: daily contact with industrial solvents and glues at the screen-printing studio for about 4 years; reports mold and moisture exposure from a damp basement storage area. Took antibiotics as a child and had high sugary intake in childhood; not born via C-section. Mercury fillings not removed. Maintains daily oral hygiene.

Trended labs (Mar 2025 to May 2026): ferritin falling 52 -> 41 -> 34 -> 18 ng/mL; iron saturation 24 -> 20 -> 16 -> 11%; vitamin D (25-OH) 31 -> 28 -> 25 -> 22 ng/mL; hs-CRP rising 0.9 -> 1.3 -> 1.7 -> 2.1 mg/L; TSH creeping up 2.8 -> 3.1 -> 3.5 -> 3.8 mIU/L. The downward ferritin trend with low iron saturation signals depleting iron stores even though ferritin is still technically low-normal.

Uploaded Quest-format lab panel (collected 2026-05-20): iron saturation 11% (LOW), UIBC 365 mcg/dL (HIGH), ferritin 18 ng/mL (low-normal, trending down), 25-OH vitamin D 22 ng/mL (LOW), hs-CRP 2.1 mg/L (elevated), calculated LDL 112 mg/dL (HIGH), TSH 3.8 mIU/L (high-normal). HbA1c 5.4%, ApoB 88 mg/dL, estradiol 48 pg/mL. Interpretation: depleting iron stores with low iron saturation and high UIBC, insufficient vitamin D, mild systemic inflammation, and a high-normal TSH worth screening.

OURA Ring trends: 90-day baseline averaged sleep 7.1h, HRV 48ms, resting HR 61 bpm, readiness 82. Over the past 6 months these declined steadily; the last 21 days averaged sleep 5.5h (-22% vs baseline), HRV 38ms (-21%), resting HR up about 7 bpm to 68, readiness 64. The long-term decline reveals a pattern that a single reading would miss.

Practitioner pre-visit follow-up questions (Dr. Okafor, generated 2026-05-22): (1) Confirm whether the recently heavier menstrual flow correlates with the falling ferritin [hormone/iron]. (2) Ask about ventilation and PPE use in the print studio [environment/detox]. (3) Screen thyroid given high-normal TSH with fatigue; consider thyroid antibodies [hormone/thyroid].
